scope: All 149 successful public content paths across en/is/fr/pt-br/ar; 153 successful HTML URLs including four version-query aliases
Production English article/search runtime and Chromium accessibility tree

findings.summary: Added-version badges have insufficient text contrast in the light theme.
findings.fix: Use a darker teal foreground or lighter badge background that reaches at least 4.5:1 for the 14.4px badge text; verify all badge variants in both themes.
findings.evidence: Production manage-pages, reports, content-checks and account-settings: foreground #007d7e on #e0eff0 = 4.19:1; text is 14.4px. axe-core 4.11.1 confirms the failure.

findings.summary: Links inside light-theme note and warning panels fail the 4.5:1 text contrast requirement.
findings.fix: Give alert-content links a darker foreground that reaches 4.5:1 against both #e0eff0 and #e6e3f1, while retaining an underline and distinct hover/focus states.
findings.evidence: Production manage-users-and-roles and promote-search-results: #007d7e on #e0eff0 = 4.19:1. manage-snippets warning link: #007d7e on #e6e3f1 = 3.92:1. Text is 18px normal, requiring 4.5:1.

findings.summary: The open mobile navigation lets Tab move to background controls that the menu completely covers.
findings.fix: Close the mobile navigation when focus moves outside its toggle and navigation, or implement an accessible modal menu with background inertness, focus containment, Escape dismissal and focus restoration. Keep the toggle available to close the menu.
findings.evidence: Live Chromium at 390×844: Space opens the menu; after 44 navigation links, Tab focuses Light mode, Copy page, copy options and English behind nav.primary-nav.is-visible. Their centres hit the opaque menu, while aria-expanded stays true. Escape leaves the menu open. See raw/keyboard-mobile.json.

findings.summary: Search and 404 pages have an empty document language.
findings.fix: Use the active Django LANGUAGE_CODE as a fallback when self.locale.language_code is absent, and verify blank/results/empty search pages and nonexistent URLs in English and translated locales.
findings.evidence: 404 GET /en/a11y-audit-nonexistent-page/ renders <html lang="">; root browser evidence raw/states.json confirms empty document language in blank/results/empty search pages too. These views lack a page instance.
findings.component: Shared base template / search and 404 views

findings.summary: Substantial English fallback content inherits the translated page language without a language override.
findings.fix: Translate fallback content, or explicitly mark English introductions/article blocks and other English passages lang=en while retaining the correct language for translated UI. Track the actual language of CMS translation segments so templates can render accurate language attributes.
findings.evidence: /fr/ lang=fr: introduction begins Welcome to the Wagtail user guide; /is/reference/content-checks/ lang=is: English Content quality checks are present in the CMS paragraph; /pt-br/how-to-guides/manage-forms/ lang=pt-br: English Wagtail provides a flexible form builder paragraph; /ar/about/ lang=ar: English The User Guide is a website paragraph. None has lang=en ancestors.
findings.component: Untranslated CMS segments / multilingual fallback content

findings.summary: Asynchronous search result counts and no-results messages are not exposed as status messages.
findings.fix: Give the persistent count container role="status" and aria-atomic="true"; update a stable text node after the latest search finishes, announce loading for prolonged requests, and avoid making the entire result list live.
findings.evidence: Independent production query page returns 3 results found and 3 anchors; focus stays on #search and live regions are empty. Zero-result states likewise use a plain heading. main.js:28–43 updates counts without status semantics.

findings.summary: The visible feedback-rating acknowledgement lacks status semantics.
findings.fix: Add a persistent status region outside replaceable feedback/form content; announce rating receipt and successful comment submission after checked successful responses, and expose failures with an accessible retry path.
findings.evidence: Mocked rating-success runtime confirms a plain Thanks for your feedback! span and no live regions. Source comment submission removes its form at line 67 without a confirmation; this separate outcome omission is a usability concern.

findings.summary: The Icelandic page-tools row overflows the 320px viewport and pushes the language control offscreen.
findings.fix: Allow the shared page-tools flex row to wrap or stack at narrow widths; ensure each control can shrink or wrap translated text and remain fully operable within 320 CSS px. Verify long translations with text spacing and enlarged text.
findings.evidence: Independent production verification: /is/ document scrollWidth 347 at viewport320, increasing to414 with WCAG text spacing; /is/how-to/finding-your-way-around/ 323→395. The overflowing element is the Íslenska language-selector toggle.

findings.summary: The mobile navigation toggle advertises an ARIA menu popup although its content is ordinary navigation.
findings.fix: Remove aria-haspopup=true from this disclosure button; retain the updated aria-expanded state and optionally add aria-controls pointing to an ID on the navigation container. Keep native navigation links instead of adding menu roles.
findings.evidence: The toggle has aria-haspopup=true (equivalent to menu), but opens <nav class=primary-nav><ul> with ordinary links rather than a menu widget. mobile-menu/index.js correctly updates aria-expanded.

findings.summary: The visually highlighted current navigation page is not identified programmatically.
findings.fix: When matching the current pathname, set aria-current=page on that link alongside the active class. Ensure exactly the current page link is marked.
findings.evidence: On /en/how-to-guides/manage-pages/ the link has class navigation__link active; CSS changes its background and foreground. Its Chromium AX properties contain URL/focusable only, with no current state.

findings.summary: The light/dark toggle exposes neither its selected state nor a changing action name.
findings.fix: Use a native checkbox or button role=switch with aria-checked, or a toggle button with aria-pressed and stable Dark mode name; synchronize initial and changed state in blocking.js. Alternatively announce the next action with a changing button name.
findings.evidence: Chromium AX tree before/after click exposes the same button name Toggle between dark and light theme and no checked/pressed state; body.theme-dark changes false to true. aria-label overrides the CSS-switched inner Light mode/Dark mode text.

findings.summary: The theme switch becomes visually indistinguishable from its background in forced-colors mode.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors style using system colors and a visible border or system-color icon so the switch and its state remain discernible; retain native color adjustment where possible.
findings.evidence: Chromium forcedColors: active on production homepage: switch background, ::before and ::after all rgb(255,255,255), border 0px none; no visible switch boundary or thumb remains.

findings.summary: On full search pages, the modal Search label is associated with the main-page input instead of its own input.
findings.fix: Use distinct ids such as page-search and modal-search, updating each label for attribute to match its respective input. Preserve the modal data-search-input selector and search query field name.
findings.evidence: Live /en/search/?query=pages contains two input#search elements. The main input.labels contains both Search labels; modal input.labels is empty. Opening the modal exposes textbox "Search…" from its placeholder instead of its explicit label. See raw/forms-runtime.json.
findings.component: Full search page and search modal

findings.summary: The language selector offers Arabic translations whose unresolved URLs become relative None links and return 404.
findings.fix: Restrict language-selector translations to public, routable pages and resolve each URL before rendering; omit unavailable translations or link explicitly to a valid locale landing page. Reuse the existing hreflangs URL-validation approach.
findings.evidence: 43 distinct crawled successful pages expose an Arabic link with href="None", across English, Icelandic, French and Portuguese. The crawl confirms /en/getting-started/overview/None/ returns 404.

findings.summary: Copy-link and copy-prompt success changes a different control’s label without an announced status.
findings.fix: Keep copy control names stable and update a persistent role="status" aria-atomic="true" element with a concise translated success message for each copy action; retain focus on the invoking control.
findings.evidence: copy-success runtime confirms Copied! appears without live regions. Source handleCopyLink and handleCopyPrompt call showFeedback(this.copyPage), changing a different button from the invoking control for 2000ms.

findings.summary: The open search dialog has no accessible name, so assistive technology cannot identify its purpose as a dialog.
findings.fix: Give the dialog an accessible name with a translated aria-label="Search", or add a visible Search heading and reference its id with aria-labelledby. Retain the separate Search label for the input.
findings.evidence: Production open state: <div id="search-modal" tabindex="-1" aria-modal="true" role="dialog"> has no aria-label or aria-labelledby. Chromium accessibility snapshot begins "- dialog:" with no name; textbox alone is named Search. Explicit axe aria-dialog-name run fails.

findings.summary: Feedback tooltips disappear when the pointer moves from their button onto the tooltip content.
findings.fix: Keep the tooltip visible while the pointer is over either its trigger or tooltip and provide Escape dismissal; consider visible helpful/not helpful labels that remove the need for explanatory hover content.
findings.evidence: Live Manage pages: hovering Happy displays This page was helpful. Moving the pointer into the tooltip rectangle (691,387;170×33) removes it within 500ms; Escape while hovering leaves it visible. Keyboard focus alone does not reveal it. See raw/tooltip-runtime.json.

findings.summary: Wagtail 6.4 release topics use H3 for top-level article sections.
findings.fix: Change the five release topic headings from H3 to H2 in CMS content and the corresponding export; these topics are siblings of the contents panel, rather than subsections of its On this page heading.
findings.evidence: The page uses H1 New in Wagtail 6.4, H2 On this page, then H3 Previews for StreamField Blocks, Alt text management enhancements, Drag-and-drop reordering for StreamField, Search terms report, Additional user interface improvements.

findings.summary: Repeated navigation landmarks have no distinct accessible names.
findings.fix: Label primary navigation and previous/next navigation distinctly; remove the unnecessary nav wrapper around the standalone skip link or give it a distinct name. Verify landmark navigation exposes clear purposes.
findings.evidence: English home has <nav class="skip-link"> and <nav class="primary-nav" data-mobile-menu>; content pages also have <nav class="nav-buttons">. None has aria-label or aria-labelledby.

findings.summary: The current-status reference link leads to a removed English URL and returns 404.
findings.fix: Update the CMS source and exported Markdown link to the current page-status reference location, and provide a redirect from /en/reference/page-status-definitions/ where practical.
findings.evidence: Production /en/how-to-guides/find-your-way-around/ links current status of the page to /en/reference/page-status-definitions/; the crawl records status 404 for that URL.

findings.summary: The French homepage Guides pratiques card leads to a missing French section and returns 404.
findings.fix: Publish the French how-to section or update the CMS card to a valid translated destination; suppress links to unavailable sections until a usable landing page exists.
findings.evidence: Production /fr/ exposes a Guides pratiques card linking to https://guide.wagtail.org/fr/how-to-guides/; the live crawl records HTTP 404 for that destination.

passed: 200% text resize through root font-size enlargement on homepage, overview and manage-pages retained content without horizontal scrolling or clipped visible text.
Across 425 rendered image instances on distinct successful URLs, all images have an alt attribute; 393 are nonempty and 32 are empty. English sitemap images have nonempty alternatives.
All 153 successful HTML URLs have one H1 and one main landmark; all 149 successful content paths were inspected across five locales.
All internal fragment targets referencing crawled pages resolve to recorded heading IDs; #main-content is handled by the skip-link audit.
All successful HTML pages have nonempty document language appropriate to the selected locale; search/404 absence and untranslated passages are reported separately.
All successful HTML titles identify their page topic; duplicate English titles across locale copies identify the same topic and were not treated as independent title failures.
Arabic home and article pages have dir=rtl; Icelandic, French and Brazilian Portuguese successful pages declare their respective language codes.
Bootstrap adds role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" and removes aria-hidden="true" when opening the production search modal; missing static role is not a runtime defect.
Both feedback buttons are reachable in sequence by Tab without submitting feedback.
Content-copy controls correctly use buttons for copying and anchors for navigating to Markdown resources.
Copy and language dropdown triggers initialize aria-expanded=false; Bootstrap dropdown owns state transitions.
Copy options and language dropdowns open with Enter, ArrowDown reaches their first item, and Escape closes and restores focus to their trigger.
Copy page activates with Enter, preserves focus, displays Copied!, and writes the expected page Markdown to the clipboard (16,140 characters on Manage pages).
Crawled link inventory has no empty links without an aria-label, and no standalone click here/read more/learn more links.
Escape dismissal and backdrop dismissal both close the search modal and restore focus to the search trigger.
Existing CI runs frontend build/lint/Vitest and Django checks/backend coverage with PostgreSQL; mobile-menu tests assert aria-expanded changes.

Feedback reveal and completion were exercised with every POST intercepted and fulfilled locally; no production feedback was submitted. After the initial buttons are removed, the next Tab reaches the newly revealed textarea; after Submit is removed, the next Tab reaches the following footer link.
Feedback textarea has a programmatically associated Your feedback label; happy and unhappy native buttons expose names within the visible Was this page helpful context.
Generated pilcrow section links are inside their corresponding heading and inherit programmatically determined heading context; ambiguous standalone names alone do not fail 2.4.4 AA.
Global 2px focus outline overrides theme-toggle outline removal via !important.
Home SectionGridBlock renders heading-and-description cards with CSS layout, not tabular data requiring row/column header associations.
Independent modal search with query page returns 3 results and retains input focus; status-region absence corroborates LIVE-001.
Inspected all 156 available crawl records: no data-table elements were recorded and no table/list/grid axe violations appeared.
Main body, shared navigation, footer and native search input retain readable foreground/background combinations in sampled light and dark states.
Main-page search input and Search submit button are native keyboard-operable controls with accessible names.
Manage pages table-of-contents links activate with Enter; the next Tab advances within the destination section.
Markdown and llms text links describe the resource format in their visible names.
Mobile navigation expanded state is updated on open and close in source and captured runtime.
Navigation, copy-options and language-options templates use native ul/li list markup; page search results use native ul/li markup.
No additional broken heading relationships were asserted solely from heading-level changes; Wagtail 6.4 section hierarchy remains an advisory finding.
No authored broken aria-labelledby/aria-describedby/aria-controls references were found in scoped templates.
No iframe/video/audio elements were found in successful guide pages.

No personal-information fields, authentication, required user-data fields or multi-step repeated-entry process were found in these forms; autocomplete and redundant-entry requirements are not applicable to the search query or free-text comment.

No public authentication, drag-only interaction, checkout, multi-step repeated-entry process, user-facing time limit, or audio/video embed was identified in inspected public guide flows; Wagtail admin features described by documentation are outside the guide website interaction scope.

Parsed all available saved page and state HTML for actual table elements and role=table/grid/treegrid: none found. JavaScript strings inside injected axe scripts were excluded from markup interpretation.
Representative homepage, section, overview, manage-pages and 404 layouts fit 320 CSS px without horizontal scrolling.
Responsive dark-desktop/320px-light scans reviewed for 153 URLs; all repeated findings are consolidated by source cause.
Runtime inventory reviewed for 196 actual HTML URLs (153 successful, 43 404), excluding synthetic plaintext wrappers.
Search dialog opening moves focus to the labelled search input.
Search error handling uses a native alert rather than a silent console-only branch; error dialog behavior was reviewed in source only.
Search result links are keyboard reachable and dropdown options support ArrowDown and Escape with focus restoration.
Search trigger keyboard activation focuses the Search input; Shift+Tab in the empty dialog returns to that input without reaching background controls.
Search updates are debounced by 150ms rather than firing a request for every immediate keyboard event.
Server-rendered full search pages are navigation results and do not require their initial counts to be live regions.
Shared controls use native buttons, links and text inputs rather than custom div roles.
Shared decorative icons use aria-hidden=true with parent text or accessible names.
Shared logo, section illustrations, alert icons, footer icons and feedback emoji use aria-hidden=true with adjacent text or named parent links/buttons.
Shared navigation, table-of-contents, section cards and article cross-links use descriptive destination names.
Source review found no positive tabindex or non-native click-only interactive elements in the scoped components; inspected keyboard targets receive a 2px solid focus outline.
Source templates and content block definitions contain no data-table, interactive-grid, treegrid, sortable-table or table-pagination implementation.
Tests cover locale behavior, header content, 404 responses, content rendering and heading fragment-link generation.
The mobile menu opens with Enter and Space, updates aria-expanded, and its native navigation links are keyboard reachable; closed navigation is display:none and excluded from Tab order.
The modal Search input is explicitly labelled on pages without a competing full-page search form.
The search trigger opens with Enter, focuses the input, makes search result links keyboard reachable, and Escape closes the modal and restores trigger focus.
The skip link is the first Tab stop, becomes visible, and Enter followed by Tab reaches a main-content link in production Chromium.
Theme toggle and sampled standalone controls meet 24 CSS px target size; short inline content links use the inline-text exception.

This audit includes source review, production HTML/axe scans, keyboard interaction, Chromium accessibility-tree inspection, mocked feedback submissions, and responsive/theme/accessibility preference checks documented in raw evidence.

WCAG text-spacing override (line height 1.5, letter spacing .12em, word spacing .16em, paragraph spacing 2em) on homepage, overview, manage-pages and reference layouts caused no main-content overflow.

notes.note: Coverage: crawl completed 238 navigations resulting in 197 unique final addresses: 153 successful HTML URLs (149 content paths plus four query aliases), 43 HTML 404 addresses and one plaintext .md resource. The synthetic browser wrapper for .well-known/agent-skills/wagtail-guide-support/SKILL.md was excluded from HTML structure checks.
Heading levels and landmark labels reported as n/a are structural improvements, not independently proven WCAG AA failures.

No screenshots were captured or inspected. Image alternatives were reviewed textually and against surrounding instructional prose; pixel-level equivalence and screenshot transcription completeness were not established.

32 empty-alt instructional image instances occur on 15 Icelandic/Brazilian Portuguese paths. Many have adjacent prose explaining the same action, so empty alt alone was not asserted as WCAG 1.1.1 failure. Editors should verify equivalent information: /is/releases/new-in-wagtail-4-1/ explicitly refers to looking at the preceding snippets screenshot; /is/how-to/finding-your-way-around/ and /pt-br/how-to-guides/find-your-way-around/ have seven and five empty-alt screenshots respectively; /is/tutorials/getting-started/ and /pt-br/getting-started/overview/ omit sign-in image descriptions.
Short alternatives such as Pin toolbar and page history replace current draft merit contextual editorial review, but no unsupported alternative-text inadequacy failure was asserted.

The language-of-parts finding concerns clearly English sentences/paragraphs, not single-word language names, product names, code or technical terms exempted by 3.1.2. Additional English fallback navigation/footer/control strings should be covered by the same translation remediation.
content/en/index.md contains an external Wagtail developer-documentation HTML export unlike the production guide home. Its markup was not used as production home evidence.

Detailed runtime evidence is raw/crawl.json and raw/page-46.html (French home), raw/page-70.html (Portuguese forms), raw/page-100.html (Icelandic content checks), raw/page-155.html (Arabic about). raw/structure-crawl.json provides the initial 45-English-page inventory.
Search modal dialog name/focus behavior and live-region behavior are owned by separate domain specialists and are not duplicated here.

Duplicate search IDs do not produce an absent Chromium accessible name: placeholder fallback names the modal field. The finding concerns the demonstrably broken explicit label relationship under 1.3.1, not removed WCAG 4.1.1.

Language names in the selector use hreflang but no lang; adding lang to each localized label improves pronunciation. Single-word language names are not asserted as a clear 3.1.2 failure because that criterion has exceptions for proper names and indeterminate words.
On-page contents are ordinary native fragment links; no custom tree, tab or menu semantics are needed.
No screenshots captured or inspected; runtime evidence consists of DOM and Chromium accessibility-tree data.
Broken modal search label relationship is confirmed in raw/aria-runtime.json and reported by forms-specialist, avoiding duplicate issue counts.
No screenshots were taken. Runtime evidence is saved in raw/visual-runtime.json, raw/visual-extra.json and raw/visual-zoom-search.json.
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce leaves the theme-switch .25s transition active. This is an enhancement opportunity, not an asserted WCAG AA failure for this brief user-triggered transition.
200% resize was tested with doubled root text size, not manual browser zoom.
Search input was inspected in both themes; autocomplete result styling should be corroborated by the dedicated search interaction audit.

Duplicate ids are reported for their confirmed label-association consequence under 1.3.1; WCAG 2.2 removed 4.1.1, and the modal textbox still has a placeholder-derived name, so it is not reported as nameless under 4.1.2.

Feedback controls are removed while focused, causing document.activeElement to become BODY; Chromium preserves the next sequential Tab location. Explicit focus on the newly revealed textarea or a completion message would improve continuity, but this test does not establish a separate 2.4.3 failure.
Dynamic feedback and search-result announcements are handled by live-region-controller and are not duplicated here.

Feedback JS catches network errors by logging to the console, and updateFeedback does not inspect HTTP response.ok before deleting the comment interface. Production server validation/error responses were not induced; error identification and recovery remain source-review limitations.
No screenshots captured. Runtime evidence is saved to raw/forms-runtime.json, including both intercepted mock POST bodies.
No screenshots were captured. Runtime evidence is in raw/keyboard-runtime.json, raw/keyboard-mobile.json and raw/keyboard-widgets.json.
Feedback buttons were not activated because they POST to the production site; post-submission focus handling was reviewed in source only.
Missing Escape dismissal alone is not treated as an independent WCAG failure for a non-modal navigation disclosure; it contributes to the confirmed obscured-focus defect.
Search Tab traversal can briefly reach browser chrome (document.activeElement becomes BODY) before re-entering the input; no background page control was reached in the inspected modal sequence.
Focus geometry and event behavior were checked with Chromium; this does not establish cross-browser or screen-reader conformance.
Broken links are functional defects reported as n/a, not automatic WCAG 2.4.4 failures; their visible text still conveys intended purpose.
The None links are language-selector links, not image wrappers. apps/custom_media/image_formats.py only changes the fullwidth rendition filter.

Language names lack lang attributes despite hreflang on their destinations. Adding lang to each autonym can improve pronunciation; native language names may fall under the proper-name exception, so no unqualified 3.1.2 failure is asserted.
Shared Markdown-view links open new tabs without warning. Add a consistent visible/accessible new-tab cue as usability guidance; target=_blank alone does not establish an AA violation.
External destinations, private accounts and GitHub were not fetched.
Source and crawl inspection establish programmatic link context; native screen-reader link-list output was not tested.

Finalizing pass examined 220 currently available crawl records and all successful-page link inventories; no unresolved internal heading fragments or standalone click here/read more/learn more/here links were found. Crawl may still add records.
French section link is an additional functional broken destination, separate from unresolved language-selector None URLs.

Supplemental feedback-tooltip behavior was explicitly requested with this link pass and is included here; it is a pointer-hover content failure under 1.4.13, independent of any missing Escape issue. No feedback request was sent during tooltip tests.

Happy/Unhappy accessible button names are interpretable with the preceding Was this page helpful question, but matching the explicit tooltip purpose (This page was helpful / This page could be improved) in visible labels and accessible names would reduce ambiguity. This is usability guidance, not a separately scored naming failure.
Runtime feedback evidence uses browser-routed mocked responses; no production feedback was submitted.
Native screen reader speech was not tested; findings establish absent required status semantics rather than measured output from a particular screen reader.

Clipboard and feedback catch branches log errors without user-visible outcomes. Clipboard failure and backend feedback errors were not exercised; add visible accessible error messages and verify error recovery.

Source search requests have neither cancellation nor a latest-request check; a late response can restore stale counts/results after another query, blanking input, or closing the dialog. Address this alongside status announcements; no standalone WCAG failure is asserted without a reproduced user impact.
Search loading is a CSS is-loading class with no status text/aria-busy. Include prolonged-loading messaging in the search-status remediation.
Confirmed mobile focus-obscuring failure is already recorded in keyboard-navigator.json as KEYBOARD-MOBILE-OVERLAY-FOCUS; it is not duplicated here.

axe-core 4.11.1 aria-dialog-name tags are cat.aria and best-practice, without WCAG tags. A WCAG-tag-only scan therefore omits it; the 4.1.2 mapping here is a manual assessment of the unnamed dialog interface.

Normative naming requirement: WAI-ARIA dialog role requires an author-provided accessible name: https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#dialog ; WCAG name/role/value context: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html .

No visible close button is supplied; Escape and backdrop dismissal work. A visible Close control would improve discoverability and touch/screen-reader operation, but its absence is not scored as an independent failure here.

Mobile toggle aria-haspopup="true" describes a menu popup although the disclosed content is ordinary navigation links; remove aria-haspopup for a navigation disclosure and consider aria-controls. This recommendation is not scored independently.
No screenshots captured. Targeted runtime and axe evidence is saved to raw/modal-specialist-runtime.json; CSP bypass was enabled only in the isolated audit browser to inject axe.
Full raw URL/node incidence retained in raw/runtime-inventory.json; do not score each repeated node separately.
Text-spacing-only horizontal overflow is retained as supporting responsive evidence rather than automatically labelled a separate 1.4.12 failure.
No screenshots and no production feedback submissions were used.
Browser automation and axe cannot establish complete WCAG conformance or replace native screen-reader testing.
Table captions, header scope/headers, merged cells, responsive data-table relationships, selection, sorting and virtual-grid keyboard operation are not applicable to the inspected production content.

Default RichTextBlock and AnnotatedTextBlock are available to editors, but no table block or custom richtext table feature was found; source capability alone does not establish inaccessible live tables.
Screenshots of Wagtail administrative listings embedded in documentation are images, not live data tables on this site; image accessibility is covered by the relevant specialist.

The production crawl was still progressing when this inventory was read; the root audit can rerun the deterministic table/list inventory against the final crawl. No screenshots or source edits were made.

Coverage is a site-wide deep inspection of discovered public routes and shared components, not proof of WCAG conformance. Report exact completed crawl and responsive counts from final raw artifacts; do not report discovered, failed or pending addresses as successfully audited.

The generated numerical score grades this finding set. It is not a percentage of WCAG criteria satisfied, certification, or evidence that unflagged content conforms. List advisory n/a findings separately from conformance failures.

Native screen-reader speech was not tested. Chromium accessibility-tree output supports role/name/state evidence but cannot establish actual NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver or TalkBack announcements. Screenshots were explicitly excluded.

Before closing remediation, test NVDA with Firefox and Chrome on Windows, VoiceOver with Safari on macOS/iOS, and TalkBack with Chrome on Android. Start with home, long Manage pages article, forms guide, a translated article, Arabic RTL home, search results and a translated 404.

Native screen-reader checklist: announce page title/language and browse headings/landmarks; follow skip link; identify current navigation page; confirm theme checked state; open mobile navigation and search; traverse overlays both directions; close and verify focus return; open search on a full search page; announce search results/no results; activate Copy page/link/prompt and verify success/failure; rate helpfulness, enter feedback and submit; verify outcome announcements and useful focus after removed controls.

Localization checklist: verify speech switches for real translated passages, RTL reading/focus order, translated control names/error messages, fallback routes and search/404 html lang. Review instructional image alternatives against source screenshots with an editor when visual inspection is permitted. Textual alt presence alone does not establish equivalent information.

Responsive checks at 320 CSS pixels approximate the reflow width associated with 400% desktop zoom, but do not replace actual browser zoom or 200% text-only zoom. Complete Firefox text-only enlargement and Chromium/Safari 200%/400% zoom checks; also test physical portrait/landscape, mobile browser zoom, focus indicators and target size/spacing.

Emulated forced-colors and reduced-motion preferences identify rendering differences but do not replace native Windows High Contrast and device tests. No flashing or required time-based task was found; animations and preference support still require review where new content is added.

Add Django assertions that normal/search/404 HTML has a valid locale language and distinct search-input IDs with correctly associated labels. Extend Vitest behavior tests to theme initial/toggled accessibility state and aria-current, alongside existing menu expanded-state assertions.

Add Playwright with @axe-core/playwright against a local Django fixture server in CI, after frontend build and database setup. Include WCAG 2.2 AA tags plus supplemental aria-dialog-name; scan initial and open states across home/article/search/404, light/dark and narrow/wide widths. Inject axe using its library with CSP handled explicitly; initial failed script injections are tooling errors, not site accessibility failures.

Add browser behavioral regressions for keyboard overlay traversal/focus visibility, modal opening on search pages, named dialogs, live count announcements, clipboard success/failure and feedback success/failure. Intercept feedback POSTs so CI and production smoke tests never create genuine feedback records.

Unit tests alone cannot measure real CSS visibility, overlap, contrast, reflow or accessibility-tree behavior. Browser assertions should verify user-observable outcomes, not just mirror class changes.

Run a focused re-audit after each remediation group, then repeat the complete discovered-route crawl and state matrix before release. Run shared-component smoke tests on each pull request and full production content scans periodically and after major CMS content/template changes; establish persistent finding IDs for future deltas.

Applicability requires continued review: WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry and 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication currently have no identified public-guide trigger, rather than being proved universally inapplicable. Public accessibility of admin authentication is a separate scope.

Cognitive review should emphasize clear labels and instructions under 2.4.6/3.3.2, consistent shared navigation/help under 3.2.3/3.2.6 and understandable feedback/errors. Reading level under 3.1.5 is AAA and should not be presented as an AA failure.

Clipboard Copy page name mutations may be announced by some assistive technology when focused; the strongest unannounced success evidence is Copy link/prompt changing a different control. Feedback comment success removes the form without visible confirmation: distinguish that absence and focus loss from an existing visible unannounced status message.
